overview.summary: The jab is a fast lead-hand straight punch. It uses a direct hand path, coordinated shoulder movement, a stable stance, and an immediate return to guard rather than maximum force.
objectives: Move the lead fist toward the target along a direct path
Keep the rear hand protecting the guard
Maintain a stable base without excessive forward lean
Retract the lead hand promptly to the starting guard
safety: Keep the wrist aligned with the forearm
Do not forcefully lock the elbow at full extension
Practise with clear space and controlled speed

principles.title: Direct hand path
principles.explanation: The lead fist travels forward with minimal unnecessary sideways movement. A shorter path generally makes the action easier to control and retract.

principles.title: Controlled elbow extension
principles.explanation: The elbow extends behind the fist while remaining short of a forceful lock. The wrist, elbow, and shoulder should support the direction of the strike.

principles.title: Stable base
principles.explanation: The stance supports the movement while the torso stays controlled. Reaching with the upper body can move the body beyond its comfortable base of support.

principles.title: Coordinated movement
principles.explanation: The fist, elbow, shoulder, torso, and stance contribute as a sequence rather than as isolated parts. The goal is efficient timing, not unnecessary tension.

principles.title: Immediate recovery
principles.explanation: After extension, the fist returns along a controlled path and the guard is restored. Recovery is part of the technique, not an action added afterward.

principles.title: How to interpret force
principles.explanation: Punching force depends on mass, acceleration, timing, contact, and whole-body coordination. A camera can describe visible motion but does not directly measure impact force or joint torque.
